Score 80-100 for articles directly covering: news and events in Williams Lake, Quesnel, 100 Mile House, Bella Coola, Horsefly, Likely, Anahim Lake, Alexis Creek, or the Cariboo Regional District; local government and civic decisions (City of Williams Lake, City of Quesnel, CRD, District of 100 Mile House); local health services and emergency closures; local economy, businesses, and community programs; Cariboo arts, culture, and community events; AND digital equity, rural internet access (fiber, fixed wireless, Starlink), and connectivity serving these specific communities. Score 20-49 for: general BC news that may affect rural areas, broader rural Canada topics without specific Cariboo tie-in. Score 0-19 for: national/international news without Cariboo relevance, pure tech or entertainment with no community angle. Penalise heavily (score 0–20): international geopolitical and war news with no Cariboo tie-in; science discoveries without a local community connection; consumer tech reviews and gadget guides; wildlife and conservation stories not involving Cariboo communities or First Nations; BC provincial news without direct Cariboo-region relevance. Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

items.title: [theglobeandmail.com] B.C. voters cast ballots in close race as officials hand-count votes
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

British Columbia voters are choosing a 93-member legislature Saturday in a snap provincial election called two years early, with the governing New Democratic Party (NDP) and the Conservative Party of B.C. running close in final polls. During the campaign, Premier David Eby acknowledged frustration over the early election call, while both major parties promoted competing plans on affordability, health care and the economy. Eby initially cited U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade threat as a reason to seek a new mandate, then said he should have explained more clearly that the legislature had stalled under the NDP’s narrow majority. Eby also accused interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson of serving as a “Trojan horse” for extremists in his party; Doerkson called that characterization “absurd”. Election officials will count election-day ballots by hand because the snap vote left Elections BC too little time to prepare enough tabulators. Officials will electronically tabulate advance-voting and electoral-office ballots and report those results first. Absentee and mail-in ballots will not be included in election-night totals; they are scheduled for the final count from Nov. 6 to Nov. 10.

items.title: [MacRumors] Apple Ordered to Open iPhone to Rival App Stores in Australia
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Australia's Federal Court today ordered Apple to allow competing app stores, direct app downloads, and alternative payment services for Australian users from March 1, 2027.


The orders follow the court's August 2025 finding that Apple misused its market power by restricting app distribution and payment options. They cover users whose Apple Account region is Australia, with Apple Developer Program members worldwide able to participate.

Apple must let users find, download, install, and update apps through competing marketplaces and websites without charging for access or obstructing their use. Developers must receive the necessary tools on substantially the same terms as for App Store distribution, and Apple cannot penalize them for using competing stores or payment services.

Developers will also be able to offer alternative payments and link to other ways to pay, including within ‌App Store‌ apps. Apple cannot require them to offer its own purchasing system alongside alternatives, report those transactions, or allow Apple to audit them. Developers can offer lower prices through competing payment services without Apple preventing them.

The ruling also limits Apple's ability to collect fees on those purchases. It cannot charge for purchases through alternative payment services or websites in apps distributed outside the ‌App Store‌. For ‌App Store‌ apps, fees are capped at the equivalent charge for payments for physical goods or services, plus any genuine, reasonable additional costs Apple incurs for digital purchases.

Apple also cannot make alternative distribution conditional on developers offering content purchased elsewhere through its own payment system.

Security checks will remain. Apps downloaded outside the ‌App Store‌ must undergo an automated security or privacy scan and be notarized by Apple or a qualified third party. However, Apple cannot impose disproportionate installation barriers or otherwise obstruct alternative distribution. Additional security requirements for competing payments must be necessary and proportionate, with developers given an explanation in advance.

Apple can remove or disable externally installed apps only in specified cases involving harmful content, genuine security risks, or legal requirements. It cannot ban third-party apps or alternative app stores from being preinstalled on iPhones, but does not have to distribute competing stores through the ‌App Store‌.

Apple told Reuters that it plans to appeal the ruling and ask the court to pause its enforcement, citing its intellectual property rights and ‌App Store‌ security.

The changes take effect at noon Melbourne time on March 1, 2027. Apple can apply between February 1 and February 15, with supporting evidence, for a court-approved extension until May 3.

items.title: [agrifocusafrica.com] Uganda targets 10,000 tractors in five-year mechanization push
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Uganda plans to deploy 10,000 tractors over five years to expand mechanized farming, Agriculture Minister Frank Tumwebaze told Parliament on Oct. 21. The strategy proposes 21 mechanization centers and a cost-sharing model involving the government, commercial farmers and producer groups. Tumwebaze said dependence on manual labor and unpredictable weather constrain productivity, while machinery could help farmers cultivate more land and support value-added production. Kubota and autonomy-software company Agtonomy are extending a pilot to automate orchard work such as spraying, mowing and underplant cultivation. In the United States, drone-treated acreage grew to 16.4 million acres in 2025. Equipment makers have also introduced higher-capacity grain conveyors designed to reduce harvest handling time.

The strategy proposes 21 mechanization centers and a cost-sharing model involving the government, commercial farmers and producer groups. Tumwebaze
items._excerpt: Uganda plans to deploy 10,000 tractors over five years to expand mechanized farming, Agriculture Minister Frank Tumwebaze told Parliament on Oct. 21. The strategy proposes 21 mechanization centers and a cost-sharing model involving the government, commercial farmers and producer groups. Tumwebaze said dependence on manual labor and unpredictable weather constrain productivity, while machinery could help farmers cultivate more land and support value-added production (agrifocusafrica.com). Kubota and autonomy-software company Agtonomy are extending a pilot to automate orchard work such as spraying, mowing and underplant cultivation (agdaily.com). In the United States, drone-treated acreage grew to 16.4 million acres in 2025. Equipment makers have also introduced higher-capacity grain conveyors designed to reduce harvest handling time (northernag.net, farmtario.com). Existing capacity: Since 2018, Uganda says it has deployed 1,080 tractors and 1,350 walk-behind tractors and trained 2,036 tractor operators and technicians (agrifocusafrica.com). Drone growth: U.S. drone-treated acreage rose 59% from 10.3 million acres in 2024 to 16.4 million in 2025, compared with 3.7 million acres in 2023 (northernag.net). Grain handling: Ontario-based Walinga says its new Agri-Belt conveyor can move grain and fertilizer at 10,000 bushels an hour; the 45-foot unit uses a standard 37-horsepower gasoline engine (farmtario.com). Harvest equipment: AGI says its LCX4 conveyor can handle up to 9,000 bushels an hour using a 60-horsepower tractor and comes in lengths from 68 to 108 feet (americanagnetwork.com).

items.title: [scotsman.com] European researchers test farm water systems as climate swings threaten crops
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Scotland’s summer of 2026 brought earlier harvests, heat stress in spring-sown crops and rapidly falling water levels, while research indicates extreme day-to-night temperature swings have become more frequent since the 1980s. Those swings can disrupt crop growth. The Scotsman reported Scottish cereal yields below historic averages, with results varying by crop, soil and location. A Swedish research project is testing a retention-irrigation system that stores water during dry periods and releases it during floods to develop recommendations for its use. In Spain, agricultural cooperatives say farmers are working to adapt and cut emissions but warn that putting innovations into practice depends on farm profitability and adequate funding under the next EU farm-policy reform.

Heat exposure: Provisional UK figures cited by The Scotsman show 40 days above 30C in summer 2026, while July received 35% of average rainfall (scotsman.com). Research funding: Spanish cooperatives participate in 14 EU projects covering resilient varieties, water efficiency and fertilizer alternatives, among other areas. Gabriel Trenzado of Cooperativas Agro-alimentarias de España said only 15% of project proposals are usually funded, compared with a 30% success rate for Spanish cooperatives (efeagro.com). Farm practices: Adaptation options described for Scottish farms include varied crop rotations, more diverse livestock grazing swards, shelterbelt hedges and trees, and drought-tolerant crop varieties (scotsman.com).

items.title: [ScienceDaily] NASA's Perseverance Mars rover finds groundwater, lakes, and hot fluids in one place
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

NASA’s Perseverance rover has uncovered a surprisingly complicated history of water in Jezero Crater. Scientists expected the crater’s Margin Unit to contain lake sediments, but instead found ancient igneous rocks that were altered by water on at least three separate occasions.
